title: Unit and integration testing with Wokwi and ESP-IDF Unity

questions.prompt: Which option states the main idea of “Unit and integration testing with Wokwi and ESP-IDF Unity” correctly?
options: Voltage pushes charge, current measures its flow, and resistance limits that flow.
Split firmware into small testable units, such as a pure function that validates an ADC raw range.
Wires appear as lines and joined connections as dots.
A resistor limits current, divides voltage, and sets a stable input level.
questions.answer: Split firmware into small testable units, such as a pure function that validates an ADC raw range.
questions.explanation: Split firmware into small testable units, such as a pure function that validates an ADC raw range.

questions.prompt: Which additional fact about “Unit and integration testing with Wokwi and ESP-IDF Unity” is accurate?
options: In a four-band code, the first two bands are digits, the third is a multiplier, and the last is tolerance.
Voltage is measured in volts, current in amperes, and resistance in ohms.

questions.explanation: ESP-IDF Unity can test C/C++ components on target or on a host

questions.prompt: Which practical detail should be considered when using “Unit and integration testing with Wokwi and ESP-IDF Unity”?
options: keep test components separate from production firmware.
A closed circuit provides a complete path from the source through the load and back.
Do not assume crossing lines are connected unless the schematic shows a junction.
questions.answer: keep test components separate from production firmware.
questions.explanation: keep test components separate from production firmware.
